subject: Staggered embeddings rollout + rerank evaluation sprint plan

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: Alicia Gomez <alicia@acmeanalytics.com>
Date: Mon, 08 Feb 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Staggered embeddings rollout + rerank evaluation sprint plan

Hi team,

Putting the cross-functional plan for Acme's embeddings -> rerank migration in one thread so we can track dependencies and blockers. High level constraints from the customer: 1) a phased backfill is required to keep query latency under 300ms, 2) vector store must be hosted in us-west, Acme will provision an Azure-managed vector DB (we think Cosmos + vector extension) but they may also test Pinecone for performance parity, and 3) they need a baseline rerank eval on a 5k query sample before we flip traffic.

Proposed timeline (rough):
- Sprint 0 (this week): access + schema mapping + mutual action plan signoff
- Sprint 1 (week 1): incremental index seed (30% of corpus), rerank eval harness + golden set labeling
- Sprint 2 (week 2): full backfill with parallelized workers, prefix caching enabled
- Sprint 3 (week 3): canary traffic (10%) and monitor regressions, then gradual cutover

Action owners (initial):
- Naomi: overall PM owner / exec updates
- Marissa: CS implementation lead / migration coordinator
- Rishi: performance and rerank eval lead (sample design, metrics)
- Laura: contracts / billing check (SLA/credits if needed)

Attachments: I've put an initial mutual_action_plan.xlsx and schema-mapping.csv in the Drive link below. Please review and add blockers by EOD tomorrow.

Naomi

Subject: Re: Staggered embeddings rollout + rerank evaluation sprint plan

Thanks Naomi — I reviewed the MAP and left comments in the Drive doc (link below). A few clarifications from implementation:

1) Access: Acme needs to provision a read-only user for our ingestion workers and an admin user for engineering to validate index integrity. Can you confirm the expected hostnames and whether VNet peering is required? If Azure-managed vector store is used, we'll need a service principal + key vault access.

2) Seed strategy: For the incremental seed we recommend starting with the most active 30% of documents (by query frequency) rather than random sampling. That reduces rerank drift risk. Rishi — can you draft the eval sample selection script (5k queries) so Alicia can sanity-check?

3) Performance guardrails: We'll enable prefix/KV caching at edge and set batch sizing to dynamic. We should capture per-route P50/P95 latency & cost breakdown during the canary. If we see >10% latency regressions on p95 we'll auto-fallback to the hosted model variant.

I'll schedule a daily 30m sync for sprint 0 to get accesses and the golden set started. Proposed time: Tue-Fri 9am PT.

-Marissa

Thanks Naomi & Marissa — appreciate the clear plan. Quick responses to the questions above:

- We'll provision two identities in the us-west-2 subscription: a service principal for ingestion (read/write limited to the vector collection) and a separate admin principal for your team to validate. No VNet peering initially; we'll provide public endpoint access with IP allowlist for Redwood workers.

- We'll start with Cosmos + vector index. Samir will run a Pinecone POC but timeline for that is after Sprint 1.

- For the 5k query sample: we'll export last 90 days of search logs and send a sanitized CSV to Rishi by EOD Wednesday. Expect some noisy queries — happy to help label a small golden set.

Attaching the signed MAP stub (I attached locally — will upload final to DocuSign).

Best,

Thanks — I got the export from Alicia this morning. Quick status and asks:

- Sample prep: I've started the 5k sample pipeline. Plan is: dedupe queries, stratify by intent (navigational/informational/transactional), then pull top candidate doc IDs per query. Sending the first 500 labeled pairs for golden set review by EOD.

- Eval metrics: we'll report NDCG@10, MRR, and the change in latency/cost per-query. Please note the initial baseline was measured on a production reranker that used 128-d embeddings; the new model uses 512-d vectors so we should expect ~1.7x storage growth. Laura — we may need to confirm the committed storage tier in the contract or propose a credit if backfill causes overages.

- Vector store considerations: the Cosmos path looks fine but we should validate consistency semantics for eventual indexing (we need strongly consistent reads for the initial golden checks). If Pinecone is chosen later, the migration path for ids and metadata is straightforward (export/import), but we'll need alignment on id namespaces.

I'll push an internal PR with the sample script and a small harness for batch rerank scoring. Next sync: daily 9am PT — I'll be on for the first three.

Rishi
